title: Filtering commutes with position annotation on literals
statement: Let $t = (\ell_0,\ell_1,\dots,\ell_{m-1})$ be a term, that is a list of literals over $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$, and let $p$ be a Boolean predicate on literals. Annotate each literal with its position to obtain the list of pairs $(\ell_i, i)$, and retain those pairs whose literal satisfies $p$; separately, retain the literals of $t$ that satisfy $p$. Then for every index $k$ that is smaller than the length of both retained lists, the literal in the $k$-th retained pair equals the $k$-th retained literal of $t$.
hypotheses_covered: t is a term (list of literals over Fin n)
p is a Boolean predicate on literals
k is below the length of the filtered position-annotated list
k is below the length of the filtered term
replaced:
The literal component of the $k$-th element of the filtered $t.\mathrm{zipIdx}$
equals the $k$-th element of the filtered term $t$.
